is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected in experimental huts (p. 1707, 1708).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for kdr (Vgsc L995F / L1014F) using Martinez-Torres et al. 1998 and Ace1R (Ace-1 G280S / G119S) using Weill et al. 2004 (p. 1709, Table 1, Table 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (p. 1709) provides allele frequencies and number tested for kdr (0.08/41 in dry season, 0.88/48 in rainy season) and Ace1R (0.01/40 and 0.40/49). Table 3 (p. 1712) reports allele frequencies and numbers tested for surviving and dead mosquitoes across three treatments.

african_field_population.evidence: Field-collected mosquitoes entering experimental huts in village VK7, Kou River valley, near Bobo-Dioulasso, southwestern Burkina Faso (p. 1708).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary field trial and experimental hut study evaluating insecticide-repellent mixtures on bed nets in 2006 (p. 1708).

sub_country_location.evidence: Village VK7, Kou River valley, near Bobo-Dioulasso, southwestern Burkina Faso (p. 1708).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary experimental hut trial conducted in 2006 with original entomological and molecular data.

supplement.evidence: All necessary allele frequency and sample size data are provided in the main text in Table 1 and Table 3.

assessment.summary: This study tested repellent-organophosphate mixtures on bed nets in experimental huts in VK7, Burkina Faso, during the dry and rainy seasons of 2006. Anopheles gambiae s.s. (M and S forms) were genotyped for kdr (L995F) and Ace-1 (G280S), with allele frequencies and sample sizes reported in untreated control huts and separately for survivors vs. dead mosquitoes exposed to different net treatments.
